rationale: This is a cosmetic denominator extension of the already-archived "Operating Cash Debt-Service Coverage" (adding dvc+prstkc to dltr), so it tests essentially the same cash-flow-to-outflow coverage mechanism with an additional near-zero-denominator instability rather than a substantively different economic idea.

The two poles use exactly complementary quantities (sstk/(sstk+dltis) = 1 − dltis/(sstk+dltis), and Δre vs NEG(Δre)), so min(r,s) − min(1−r,1−s) algebraically collapses to r+s−1 — a plain additive combination of equity-funding share and retained-earnings change with no conjunctive interaction at all, contradicting the stated design.

Scaling by gross issuance makes the score explode for firms with negligible capital raises, so the ratio largely proxies inverse issuance intensity (the well-known net-issuance anomaly) while the sales-growth numerator is signed against the documented negative growth/investment-return relation, leaving the expected positive sign poorly justified.

Economically coherent and sign-consistent (payouts unsupported by internal cash, scaled by the financing round), and a genuinely different functional form from the archived MIN-based "Externally Funded Distress Payout," though it overlaps that mechanism heavily and remains vulnerable to small-denominator noise despite winsorization.

The risk-matching mechanism is a substantively new conditioner for the debt-vs-equity funding share (unlike the archived tax-capacity version) and the multiplicative rank direction matches the negative expected sign, but the signal risks being dominated by the standalone cash-flow-volatility effect and should be checked against a volatility-only benchmark.

The product of two centered changes assigns equally high scores to payout increases with improving cash flow and to payout cuts with deteriorating cash flow — states with opposite documented return implications (dividend cuts predict low returns) — so the expression cannot represent the "alignment is good" hypothesis and its sign is ambiguous.
